programs.title: David Attenborough's Natural Curiosities
programs.desc: In each episode, David Attenborough presents two cases of natural curiosities that have something in common.

programs.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programs.desc:
Documentary filmmakers go to the most remote corners of our planet to discover the secrets of the few untouched ecosystems.From the Namib Desert to Patagonia, only a few places on Earth have remained largely unchanged.Isolated from the rest of the world, they managed to defend themselves against the most harmful effects of human interference.Life there goes on as nature intended.The creators will take viewers on an exciting journey to the last places that are paradise on earth.Amazing, breathtaking landscapes will be presented, as well as exciting behaviors of the most popular animals in the world.Each episode will feature a different unique corner of the globe - from the mysterious, fog-shrouded forests of Borneo to the lush beauty of Africa's Luangwa floodplain
Only 500 years ago, the first sailors reached the Galapagos Islands.Seeing mountain peaks shrouded in fog, picturesque beaches and creatures resembling mythical beasts, they thought they had arrived in a magical land.To get there, each colonizer had to make a thousands-kilometer journey across the Pacific.Galapagos fur lions were one of the few mammals to do this.They came here two million years ago from North American waters.Life in the Galapagos waters thrives on powerful ocean currents.The animals have long traveled underwater from the Southern Ocean.The most impressive coasts of the archipelago are located on the island of Fernandina, one of the most pristine in the world.It is called the land of dragons because 120,000 marine iguanas live here.

Documentarians start their journey high in the Andes.A chain of mountain peaks stretches along Patagonia, shaping life in this mysterious land.To the north, in their shadow, lies one of the driest and most inhospitable deserts in the world - the Atacama.This is an area of ​​over 100,000 square kilometers.In some places, rainfall has not been recorded for five hundred years.At an altitude of 4,800 m above sea levelultraviolet radiation is so strong that human skin can burn in just a few moments.However, there will be those who feel like they are in paradise here.Every spring, thousands of flamingos arrive from southern Patagonia.They land in shallow lagoons to feed on the abundant algae and brine shrimp that give them their characteristic pink color.

In the snow- and ice-covered mountains of North America, it is winter for 6 months of the year.Life is reborn here with the arrival of spring.Grizzly bears wake up from hibernation.A mother and her young must act quickly to make the most of the short period of plenty in this pristine land.At this time of year, the best opportunities for food are along the coast, where the weather is more favorable.After half a year of sleep, the female and her two young need a lot of protein.Twice a day, at low tide, a seafood buffet opens.Fresh fish look very appetizing, but their spines, used for defense, signal that it is better to skip this meal.The real prize for hungry hunters are mussels.The bear uses its paw very gently so as not to damage the mussel and press it into the ground.
